visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md. Built from components/site/v3. No mockup in this directory: the place-type class is the city/community type-card landing, not a Tetherow one-off.
competitiveTarget: Beat Zillow / Redfin / Coldwell Banker type-filtered city results. Those surfaces dump the visitor into a search grid. This page is a place-type node: leftover count and median that already back the type card, a living atlas of the parent city with the type stated in the claim, and a photographed list of that type. Unique title, canonical, ItemList when listings exist. Breadcrumb is City then type, no Home.
note: H1 is `{Type} in {Place}` and it is the page's only display-scale line: the Atlas opens under the claim wearing an eyebrow (V3Atlas headlineTone='eyebrow', subject softened to Listings so the type is not said twice). One section-0 sourced claim sentence sits under the H1 — count and price band from ONE listing_tile_mv read, worded as the address census with the map marking city limits. A V3Carousel mode=rail of photographed listings (PlaceTypeFilm; shadcn-carousel adapted) follows Atlas in the fold with price+address+beds/baths/sqft on 800x600 plates. The Atlas section is UNCONDITIONAL via PlaceTypeAtlasSection + PlaceTypeAtlasStandin. Rows and marks share one hovered key. Unknown type notFound(). Do not collide with app/cities/[slug]/[neighborhoodSlug].

tasteReview.beats: Redfin Bend single-family map (redfin.com/city/16163/OR/Bend): Atlas wins on data depth (90-day sale-density cells, city-limits caveat, MLS timestamp); it loses on map scale, on a useful price claim, and on the photographed rail matching the stated band. Better than a 69 page on the opening (one H1, one sourced sentence, listings in the first viewport).

defects.section: LISTINGS INSIDE THE BEND CITY LIMITS (Atlas)
defects.finding: On desktop the Bend polygon is a small gray island in a padded cream rectangle beside a leftover instrument stack (House checkbox, Up to any price, two ticker lines). The density map is the only original object and it is framed as a dashboard widget, not a field a visitor would stop for.

defects.section: opening claim under Single-family in Bend
defects.finding: The lead states 768 homes ask $397,000 to $11,900,000 — a band so wide it is a non-fact — then restates single-family after the H1 already named the type. Count and band belong on a scrubbable emphasis line, not a static sentence.

Five photographed houses run $469,000–$524,900 while the claim’s upper bound is $11,900,000 and Atlas just-listed Discovery West at $1,775,000. The rail does not read as the same market as the sentence or the map marks. At 375 the previous control is a North compass beside a next chevron — not the shadcn-carousel prev/next interaction.
A page already titled Single-family in Bend still shows a checked House checkbox, an internal type leftover a buyer does not need on a type URL.
The lead says 768 homes; the map legend says 496 for sale and 265 pending (761). The city-limits caveat does not explain a seven-home gap between two sourced-looking figures on the same fold.

SEO increment is not visible in these first-viewport shots, so title, JSON-LD, and crawlable asks are held at best. Inventory on the fold did improve: photographed cards now show price, address, beds, baths, and sqft inside the first screen.
